findings.title: Codex response-file matching accepts an unrelated filename
findings.observation: The Cycle 5 parser locates a later response reader with call.command.includes(request.responseFile). This is substring matching, not an exact shell argument comparison. A reader for unrelated-replay-response.json therefore qualifies as a reader for replay-response.json and its output request ID is attached to the successful replay tuple.
findings.trigger: Keep a valid timeout/replay POST that writes replay-response.json, but replace the later jq command with the same read against unrelated-replay-response.json while that unrelated file's output contains the authoritative claim request ID.
findings.impact: The verifier returns PASS even though the request ID was not read from the successful replay response. A valid client replay and an unrelated response file can still be assembled into an accepted compatibility record, violating AC-15 and the documented exact response-file correlation gate.

evidence.description: At the exact head, the reviewer changed only the jq reader from replay-response.json to unrelated-replay-response.json. The negative assertion failed because verifyClientEvidence resolved PASS with every Codex objective.
Response readers are selected with call.command.includes(request.responseFile), allowing superstrings and other unrelated path arguments.
The request ID parsed from that reader is combined with the replay request path/status and then accepted by exact claim matching.
Cycle 5 covers cross-operation, mismatched request ID and terminal status, but has no negative where the reader filename merely contains the expected response filename.
The real Codex record passes, and the SHA-bound 206-line Claude transcript prefix also passes. The failure is specifically exact response-file identity, not positive-evidence availability.
AC-15 requires each named client to actually execute the representative validation, and the plan disallows a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: Parse the response-reader command into exact arguments and require it to read the precise successful replay response-file argument; do not use substring matching. Add a negative using a longer filename that contains the expected filename, while preserving the current request-ID, status, cross-operation, body/key and live-resource checks.
findings.verification: Both current real client records still pass; all existing negatives remain closed; and changing only the jq reader from replay-response.json to unrelated-replay-response.json fails with CLIENT_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED_TRANSCRIPT.
